title: Write a book class
prompt: Complete the class `Book`. The constructor takes a title and a number of pages and stores them in `Title` and `Pages`. `Finished` starts as false, and `MarkFinished()` sets it to true. `Describe()` returns `"Dune (400 pages)"` for a book that is not finished and `"Dune (finished)"` for one that is.
hints: Which members does the constructor have to fill in, and from which parameters?
Property names start with a capital letter and parameter names do not. Title = title; stores the parameter in the property.
In Describe, test Finished. Return the title with "(finished)" when it is true, and with the pages when it is false.
checkLabels: Title must hold the title passed to the constructor.
Pages must hold the pages passed to the constructor.
A new book must not be finished.
A book that is not finished must describe itself as "Dune (30 pages)".
A book with 0 pages must still show its pages.
After MarkFinished(), Finished must be true.
A completed book must describe itself as "Dune (finished)".

wrongAnswers.misconception: Forgets to store one constructor parameter.
Describes a finished book the same way as an unfinished one.

feedback: Check each member in turn: what the constructor stores, what MarkFinished changes, and which text Describe returns for each value of Finished.
